recent_posts.title: Core Control for Execution, Lots of Fixes
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch v5.21 has been released with a new 'Control Cores Used For Test Execution' setting that pins test processes to specific CPU cores, improving predictability in resource-constrained environments at the cost of potential underutilization. The release also adds support for JetBrains Rider 2026.1, drops support for Visual Studio 2010-2015, and includes numerous bug fixes primarily targeting Rider.

recent_posts.title: Visual Studio 2026
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio 2026 preview has been released after a 4-year gap, featuring extensive AI tooling improvements with Copilot integration. Microsoft continues migrating VS components from .NET Framework to newer .NET platforms. NCrunch has already added full support for VS2026 in their v5.18 release, just 4 days after the preview launch, thanks to Microsoft's strong backwards compatibility.

recent_posts.title: Rider 2025.1, MSTest v3.8, More fixes
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch v5.13 has been released, introducing support for JetBrains Rider 2025.1 and MSTest v3.8. The new version aligns with the latest Rider improvements and adds key MSTest v3.8 features, including DataRow tests using generics and the RetryAttribute. The release also brings support for .slnx files and includes various fixes and improvements.

recent_posts.title: Fixes Fixes Fixes
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch v5.12 has been released, focusing on stability and performance fixes. Key updates include compatibility with Xunit v3.1.1.0, a restructure of the file synchronization system, support for using the NCrunch console tool without Visual Studio by leveraging the .NET SDK, and various fixes for Jetbrains Rider. Enhancements in this release aim to reduce resource overhead and improve integration experiences.

recent_posts.title: Rider 2024.3 Support, VS and Xunit fixes
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch v5.11 has been released, offering support for JetBrains Rider 2024.3, Visual Studio 2022 17.12, and adjustments for Xunit v3. This build addresses compatibility issues caused by recent updates to these tools, ensuring stable integration and performance. Users should download the latest NCrunch version marked as tested for their specific Rider version, and it is recommended to install via JetBrains Market for automatic compatibility. The update also changes how NCrunch handles Xunit binaries to avoid instability, aligning with recent updates from Xunit.

recent_posts.title: Xunit v3 Support and continued fixes
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch v5.10 has been released, featuring numerous fixes and improvements. A significant addition in this release is the new Xunit v3 test adapter, built from the ground up for the upcoming Xunit v3 RTM release. This update aims to enhance stability and transition Rider support out of beta. Full release notes are available on the download page.

recent_posts.title: Fixes and Improvements for V5 Release
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch V5 has had a successful launch with major new features like JetBrains Rider support and RDI. The recent 5.4 release focuses on fixing issues and improving performance, especially for async methods in RDI and DPI scaling in Rider. The team plans to continue enhancing V5's stability and is working on making the Rider plugin available on the JetBrains Marketplace.

recent_posts.title: NCrunch V5 Now Available
recent_posts.summary: NCrunch version 5, the largest release in its history, is now available. It introduces two major features: support for JetBrains Rider and Runtime Data Inspection (RDI). The Rider plugin, although still in BETA, integrates with NCrunch by hosting the engine outside the IDE and piping the UI through shared memory. RDI allows users to analyze code behavior during tests without a debugger, providing a detailed analysis system. The release notes stress the importance of users reporting bugs and performance issues to help improve the plugin and the RDI system.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Runtime Data Inspection
recent_posts.summary: The upcoming v5.0 release introduces Runtime Data Inspection (RDI), a new feature in NCrunch aimed at improving code analysis. Unlike traditional debugging, RDI captures extensive data during code execution and stores it in a log for post-run analysis. This allows for deeper insights into code behavior, performance bottlenecks, and variable states, facilitating easier troubleshooting. Key features include dynamic data updates, distributed processing, and aggregation of test results. While it can generate large logs and consume significant resources, RDI promises to boost productivity, especially for long-running tests and UI element renderings.

recent_posts.title: Dotnet build support. JetBrains Rider support coming soon!
recent_posts.summary: A new version of NCrunch fully integrated with JetBrains Rider will be released in about a month. The integration faced challenges due to the different technologies used by Rider and NCrunch's dependency on Winforms and WPF. The pandemic allowed the team to focus on new features, and a tool called 'wormhole' from JetBrains facilitated the UI integration. The NCrunch engine was also migrated to .NET 6 while maintaining backward compatibility with older .NET versions. Version 4.19 has been released as a maintenance update, including preliminary .NET 6 integration.
